metadata.case_name: WONG YIN WA STONNIE v. LEE TAK WONG

plaintiff.occupation_before: traffic police officer on motorcycle duty

source: he suffered left knee sprain injury as a result because his left foot stepped on the ground too hard.
left knee was swollen but the X-ray confirmed no fracture at the left knee.
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of other or unspecified parts of knee

manifestations.description: The Plaintiff needed to spend more time carrying out daily activities and could not walk or stand for a long periods. When walking up or down stairs, he would experience greater pain on left knee, which persisted for some time before the pain stopped. These discomfort and pain lasted for the first half year after the accident.
The Plaintiff currently experiences tension of the muscles of the left knee.
The Plaintiff experiences aggravated pain during rainy weather or when the weather turns cold.

When the Plaintiff wakes up from sleep, he would require support in order to keep upright. Occasionally, the Plaintiff’s sleep was disturbed throughout the night due to the pain and discomfort. As a result, his concentration and temper during the day has been affected.

Before the accident, the Plaintiff would spend time with his friends on outdoor activities such as swimming, playing football and running etc. for at least 6 or 7 times a month. However, after the accident, time spent on such activities has been significantly reduced. The Plaintiff’s social life has been hugely affected.

treatments_received: Accident and Emergency Department treatment at Kwong Wah Hospital (attended immediately after the accident)
X-ray (no fracture at the left knee)
Analgesic medication at Shun Lee Government Clinic GOPC, United Christian Hospital
Chinese bonesetter treatment and Chinese medicine (12 sessions from 6th February to 28th July 2006)

losses.description: reduced and limited mobility of the left leg; difficulty walking or standing for long periods; greater pain when walking up or down stairs

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
